title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1970-03-20
lineage: Master Reel > ? > R @ 7.5 ips > CD > EAC > WAV > FLAC

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with cleaned‑up tape hiss captures a solid early‑70 set highlighted by a scorching Lovelight and blistering Viola Lee Blues.
ai_review.review: The new SBD transfer removes much of the original hiss and brings out better instrument separation, though some distortion and low Pigpen organ levels remain. Musically the show is an above‑average early‑1970 performance with a killer acoustic set and electric highlights like Lovelight, Viola Lee Blues, Deep Elem Blues and Black Peter. Overall it’s a worthwhile listen for fans despite a few rough edges.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is judged above average (≈3.8/5) and recording quality good (≈4/5); combined weighted score yields ~4 stars. Six detailed reviews provide consistent insight.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Tape hiss markedly reduced in this transfer, but some residual hiss and occasional distortion remain; Pigpen organ is low in the mix and vocals sit forward.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong acoustic opening leads into a solid electric second set; highlights include a scorching Lovelight with memorable Pigpen rap and a blues‑heavy Viola Lee Blues, though the overall pacing is a bit uneven.

band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s vocals are loud and on key but often get buried in the mix.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ sits low in the mix, but his rap during Lovelight is a highlight; his swerling organ adds texture to Viola Lee Blues.
